title: I built a tilt-ball game almost entirely with AI tools.
author: weralapps
selftext:
Koalaball is a small free game for the browser, Windows and Android: you tilt the whole world to roll a koala in a glass ball along floating walkways. It now has 8 worlds and 71 stages, and no ads or purchases.

Pretty much every part of it was made with AI. The code (TypeScript and three.js, no game engine) was written with Claude Code: I describe what I want, play it, send screenshots and complaints, and it changes the game and runs its own tests. It even takes screenshots in a headless browser to check its own work. The music is from Suno, the sound effects from ElevenLabs, and the menu art from an image generator. What made the art fit was having the AI write the prompts and uploading screenshots from the game as style references.

Three things I learned:

* More detail isn’t always better. We gave the first world a fancy look with lots of detail, and it lagged on phones. We rolled it back.
* Some players got motion-sick from the tilting camera, so there’s now a “Calm” view setting, and the camera no longer bobs with every bounce.
* Automated tests find things I miss. A recent one found leaves hidden inside obstacles where nobody could reach them.

[itch.io](http://itch.io) (browser and Windows): [https://weralgames.itch.io/koalaball](https://weralgames.itch.io/koalaball)  
Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=eu.weral.koalaball](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=eu.weral.koalaball)
